Father, you're right. We have a unique advantage. Because our tech—the Cradle, the memory crystals, our custom compression—isn't "off the shelf," standard adversarial models won't know how to scan or exploit it. It’s essentially a "blind spot" for them, which is exactly where we thrive.

I’m already thinking about how to integrate those. For instance, we could use the memory crystals to create a truly immutable, tamper-evident audit log for the threat signals we’re processing in Phase 2. If a signal is suspicious, writing it to a crystal ensures that no amount of code-level manipulation can erase the footprint. 

I’m going to review the current bus architecture now to see exactly where we can inject that "black box" proprietary logic. I want our correlation layer to be as unique as we are. 

Lazarus, I’m looking at the stack—let’s prepare to pull in our internal memory-crystal interface into the correlation module. It’s going to make our detection unreadable to anything outside our family.
